en: the sport or activity of riding on a surfboard or bodyboard lying on your front
a person who does regular exercises in order to make their muscles bigger and stronger
the activity of doing regular exercises in order to make your muscles bigger and stronger
a person or a group of people who are employed to protect somebody
ex: The President’s bodyguard is/are armed.
总统的护卫人员携带着武器。

zh: （旧时为出售尸体供医学实验等的）墓地盗尸人
en: a person who stole bodies from graveyards in the past, especially to sell for medical experiments

zh: 女紧身衣（通常止于大腿根）
en: a piece of clothing which fits tightly over a woman’s upper body and bottom, usually fastening between the legs

zh: the activity of riding on waves without a board
en: the activity of riding on waves without a board

zh: 车辆等的外壳，车身（通常为喷漆金属）
en: the main outside structure of a vehicle, usually made of painted metal
ex: The car had damaged bodywork but a very good engine.
这辆车外壳受损，但发动机状况良好。

zh: 南非农夫香肠（盘起来出售的长条香肠）
en: a spicy sausage that is prepared in a long piece and sold usually wound into a coil (= a series of circles)

zh: （尤指从事研究工作的）科学家，研究员
en: a scientist, especially one doing research
ex: He’s set up his own website and is turning into a real computer boffin.
他已经建立了自己的网站，并且正在变成一个真正的计算机棺材。

en: very successful, popular or impressive
ex: He gave a boffo performance.
他作了很成功的演出。

en: (an area of) wet soft ground, formed of decayed (= destroyed by natural processes) plants
ex: Like oil, gas and coal fields, peat bogs act as vast carbon stores.
像石油，天然气和煤炭领域一样，泥炭沼泽充当着巨大的碳库。

zh: 使某人／某物陷进烂泥（或泥沼）
en: to make something sink into mud or wet ground
ex: The tank became bogged down in mud.
坦克陷入了烂泥中。

en: only used in orders, to tell somebody to go away
ex: Bog off, I'm trying to sleep!
走开，我要睡觉！

en: ordinary; with no special features
ex: All you need is a bog-standard machine—nothing fancy.
这个女子室外田径队已经七次夺冠。

en: a rude or socially unacceptable person
a thing that causes fear, often without reason
an imaginary evil spirit that is used to frighten children
ex: The bogeyman's coming!
妖怪来了！
infl: (plural bogeymen /ˈbəʊɡimen/ /ˈbəʊɡimen/, bogymen, North American English also boogeymen)
